title: Changing the Bill To does not change the work order's total
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, taxable at the test location's 5% tax.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer B, the payer, with its own labor rate and discount settings.
  • Have a new work order for this test, work order 1, for customer A, in Approved, that bills itself, with one part sold at $100.00, so the estimate reads Parts $100.00, tax $5.00, Total $105.00.
custom_steps:
1. Open work order 1.
  2. Open the Finance tab.
  3. Expand the Customer card.
  4. Click the Bill To field.
  5. Pick customer B in the list.
  6. Open the Finance tab.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Work order 1 opens for customer A.

Step 2:

  • The estimate shows Parts $100.00, tax $5.00 and Total $105.00 (100.00 × 5% = 5.00).

Step 3:

  • The Customer card shows a "Bill To" field under Authorizer, reading "This customer".

Step 4:

  • The list opens.

Step 5:

  • The Customer card's "Bill To" field reads customer B's name.

Step 6:

  • The estimate still shows Parts $100.00, tax $5.00 and Total $105.00: the total did not change.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Bill To", Confluence 1003585538, version 0.5 (6 Nov 2026, pending approval, Chris Ward), read 9 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-12289, story SV-12309 (Story 7, Invoicing to the Bill To)

  • S7-R3: “Pricing, tax, discounts, fees and shop supplies are the customer's; changing the Bill To never changes the total.”
  • Key Decisions: “Two customers, split by job. The customer owns pricing, tax, discounts, fees, shop supplies, history and revenue; the Bill To owns the receivable, terms, credit limit, Credit Hold, PO, deposits, payments, QuickBooks customer and IBS.”
  • Feature Overview, Core Bill To: “The customer keeps the truck, the service history, pricing, tax, discounts, fees, shop supplies and the revenue.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
